candidates.description: req.body.id is passed directly as the _id filter in a MongoDB update with multi:true. An attacker can supply an object like {"$ne":null} to match and modify all reviews.
candidates.rationale: Line 18 uses req.body.id as the _id query filter without type validation. MongoDB interprets objects as operators, so {"$ne":null} matches all documents. Combined with multi:true on line 20, a single request can overwrite every review message. The authenticatedUsers.from() call on line 16 is only used for challenge detection, not authorization.
candidates.title: NoSQL injection via MongoDB operator injection in review update

candidates.description: isRedirectAllowed uses url.includes(allowedUrl) which permits any URL that contains an allowed domain as a substring, enabling redirect to attacker-controlled hosts.
candidates.rationale: Line 136 checks url.includes(allowedUrl) instead of parsing and comparing hostnames. A URL like http://evil.com/?x=http://localhost:3000 passes the check because it contains the allowed string. This function is used to validate redirect targets, so any consumer of it is vulnerable to open redirect.
candidates.title: Open redirect allowlist bypass via substring matching

candidates.description: retrieveBasket queries BasketModel by req.params.id without verifying the basket belongs to the authenticated user, enabling horizontal privilege escalation.
candidates.rationale: Line 19 fetches the basket using only the URL parameter id with no ownership check. The challenge detection on lines 21-24 identifies cross-user access but does not block the response. Any authenticated user can enumerate basket IDs to read other users' cart contents including product names and quantities.
candidates.title: IDOR on basket retrieval allows reading any user's basket
